scope: runtime-lab capture pipes under concurrent process creation on this Rust/macOS version
finding: The original parallel preview once lacked output EOF. Deterministic interposition proved a pipe()/fcntl CLOEXEC inheritance window in this installed std implementation, with extra PIPE descriptors in an unrelated descendant.
resolution: Atomic pipe2(O_CLOEXEC) capture, unique OwnedFd ownership and explicit post-spawn Command writer release. Older macOS without pipe2 returns Unsupported. Same-interleaving matrix: 8 original failures / 8 fixed passes, lsof and syscall flag observations preserved.
follow_up: Old measured sources were preserved byte-for-byte; old data and the original failure were not overwritten.
Final validation: 20 default-parallel complete test runs, 360 test executions; 800 structured child reports; 210 new performance observations.
Fixed and verified mechanically via tools/verify_drain_fix.py.
limits: The historical single failure lacks PID/FD telemetry, so unique retrospective attribution remains unprovable. The demonstrated defect class is fixed; no claim of universal platform correctness or descendant sandboxing.

finding: Project1's original Stdio::piped capture used the same demonstrated non-atomic macOS pipe path; the correction was required in the actual delivered project.
resolution: Implemented projects/agent-runtime/src/process_macos.rs with atomic pipe2(O_CLOEXEC) capture and OwnedFd registration. Replaced all racy Stdio::piped calls. Verified with 360 test runs, 800 structured reports, 8 dyld interposer gate cases, and fresh run-04 benchmark measurements.
follow_up: All 18 tests pass in debug and release with parallel cargo test.
Chapter 15 updated with run-04 measurements and microarchitecture trace.
Old run-01 and run-02 snapshots preserved intact.
limits: macOS 27+ pipe2 dynamic detection; unsupported on older OS without pipe2 (returns structured SpawnFailed error). Non-macOS uses unverified fallback.
